title: CI/CD y seguridad de la cadena de suministro

source.legacy_id_policy: PRESERVE_STABLE_KEY; repair semantic selectors, not saved-progress identity

finding_registry.summary: Prerequisite S43 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with 5 P0; S44 cannot treat upstream artifact as trusted evidence.
You Do readiness and gate_case are self-attested/hard-coded; READY can be manufactured without artifacts.
Roadmap targets controlled CI/cloud but practice is overwhelmingly local Python predicates/parsers.
Prefix-only sha256 validation accepts malformed digests.
Artifact digest is supplied rather than measured and reverified from an artifact.
Seven-day retention is presented as a general rule instead of lab policy.
Cache key truncates a supplied lock hash and never proves it came from the lockfile.
Workflow condition coverage is self-reported, not inspected across triggers/branches/tags/forks/manual paths.
Permission/pinning figure is placed under T1-A rather than T2-A.
Any secret-scan hit is routed directly to revoke/rotate without classification or false-positive/test-secret handling.
Permission validation does not compute effective workflow/job permissions.
pin_ok is overwritten per action, so a later pinned action can hide an earlier unpinned action.
40-hex format is accepted without verifying commit identity belongs to intended action repository.
Dependency review is a learner-supplied boolean instead of check/report evidence.
Lesson incorrectly requires artifact digest == SBOM document digest == provenance subject.
Attestation validity is a boolean rather than cryptographic/policy verification.
Provenance gate omits builder/issuer, repo/workflow and source revision identity.
Provenance prose overstates generic guarantee as exact machine identity.
Truthy approved_by is treated as independent deployment approval.
Environment protection is represented by names/approvers, not enforceable protection rules.
Promotion again accepts malformed prefix-only sha256 values.
prod/production identifier terminology is inconsistent.
Canary validator accepts negative error rates and negative rollback/RTO values.
You Do canary drops migration_compatible and rollback_tested from the guided contract.
Rollback is timed but not bound to last-known-good digest/config/data.
Migration compatibility and rollback testing are self-attested booleans.
Canary relies on one error-rate threshold without minimum sample/window or second health signal.
Branch protection/check/review requirements are values/sets, not repository ruleset evidence.
signed_commits appears decoratively/inconsistently in the taught contract.
Release notes can pass with required labels but empty/non-actionable values.
T4-B PASS requires critical_failure=True; a healthy run is misclassified STOP_SILENT_FAILURE.
Missing retained evidence routes to ASSIGN_INCIDENT_OWNER even when owner already exists.
Log redaction, owner and evidence retention remain self-attested fields.
All 24 We Do exercises repeat a predicate-repair/classify/fail-closed grammar.
E3 transfer is weak because representation/context barely changes.
All eight I Do demos are local Python simulations instead of target CI procedures.
Theory playground leaks obsolete `Practica CLIP y Whisper (simulado)` through legacy id mapping.
Canonical/public CP-N4-B brief exposes stale pre-V3 section labels for S44-S47.
Visible S44 rubric differs from canonical CP-N4-B rubric without labeling/mapping itself as interim.
Self-check calls an S44 result the CP-N4-B gate although canonical gate is S47.
Authenticated S44 exam is topically current but mostly short conceptual recognition, weak for Level-4 artifact inspection.
Four roadmap-required authentic topic assessments are absent.
Resource list omits direct first-party docs for key attestation/dependency-review/secret-protection operations.
Dense unexplained English/ops vocabulary raises avoidable language load in Peruvian Spanish.
Intro conflates GitHub Action SHA pinning with Python/package dependency locking/hashing.
Attestation teaching omits the explicit least-privilege permissions required to generate GitHub attestations.
Declared `S44-permission-scope` figure is absent from FIGURES/FIGURE_DATA; FigureFrame returns null so it never renders.

runtime_counterexamples: unpinned action followed by pinned 40-hex action -> final pin_ok True
release note keys with empty values -> True
four You Do evidence flags True with no artifacts -> READY
rejected_findings: Rename legacy `multimodal` id/file: REJECTED; stable URL/progress key needs migration, not casual rename.
Require S44 to close CP-N4-B: REJECTED; canonical gate is S47.
Require a real public-cloud deployment: REJECTED; a controlled local/CI fixture can be authentic if it produces real evidence.
Caches are inherently incompatible with reproducibility: REJECTED; they are valid optimization when not treated as authority.
Full 40-hex action pinning is unnecessary: REJECTED; current GitHub secure-use guidance supports it.
Developer comments atop the TS file are learner-facing meta-leak: REJECTED; they are not rendered. The SectionView CLIP/Whisper demo is the actual leak.
